definitions.explanation: A history compiled privately rather than by the state, often preserving anecdotes and folk accounts left out of official records. Contrasted with {正史|せいし}, the authorized dynastic history.

examples.english: It is recorded in unofficial histories.

examples.japanese: {正史|せいし}にない{逸話|いつわ}が{野史|やし}に{残|のこ}る。
examples.english: Anecdotes absent from the official history survive in unofficial histories.

examples.japanese: {当時|とうじ}の{庶民|しょみん}の{暮|く}らしは、{野史|やし}から{知|し}ることができる。
examples.english: The daily life of common people of the time can be learned from unofficial histories.

notes:
Composed of {野|や} (unofficial, rustic) + {史|し} (history). A somewhat literary term.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {正史|せいし}: official history — state-compiled and authoritative, the direct antonym
- {外史|がいし}: unofficial history — a close synonym, common in the titles of historical works
